# Adjudication Task — Chapter 345

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃345화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|제아무리 무림이 살인과 폭력이 난무하는 체험 죽음의 현장이라지만, 어느 업계나 고위층이 되면 제법 격식을 차리는 법이다.
  6|
  7|‘특히 오대세가의 일원인 사천당문의 가주쯤 되면 더더욱 그렇고.’
  8|
  9|그런 면에서 당사독은 직설적으로 말할 수는 있어도, 직설적으로 듣는 것에는 익숙하지 않은 사람이었다.
 10|
 11|바로 지금처럼.
 12|
 13|“만독지환 좀 빌려주십시오.”
 14|
 15|“……!”
 16|
 17|생각지도 못한 한 방.
 18|
 19|찰나의 순간, 눈꼬리를 파르르 떤 그가 입을 열었다.
 20|
 21|“아직도 그따위 허무맹랑한 이야기를 믿나? 젊은 줄은 알았지만 한참이나 어린놈이군.”
 22|
 23|“방금 눈꼬리 떠시는 거 봤는데요.”
 24|
 25|“헛소리!”
 26|
 27|“괜히 찔리니까 목소리 커지죠?”
 28|
 29|“아니라고 하지 않았느냐!”
 30|
 31|“어어, 주먹 쥐죠?”
 32|
 33|“없다니까!”
 34|
 35|“주머니 털어서 나오면 제가 가져도 됩니까?”
 36|
 37|“그래! 뒤져 봐라! 만약 뒤져서 안 나오면 네놈 모가지를 대신 집어넣겠다!”
 38|
 39|“아, 다른 곳에 숨겨 두셨나 보네. 그럼 취소하겠습니다.”
 40|
 41|“이익……!”
 42|
 43|“손해……!”
 44|
 45|“이 쳐 죽일 놈이 감히!”
 46|
 47|아, 마지막은 참을걸.
 48|
 49|환상적인 콤보 연타에 얻어맞은 당사독의 눈동자가 회까닥 뒤집힌다.
 50|
 51|나는 그가 암기를 뿌리기 전에 서둘러 외쳤다.
 52|
 53|“한 번! 딱 한 번만 빌려주시면 된다니까요!”
 54|
 55|“없다고 하지 않았더냐!”
 56|
 57|“그럼 없다고 치고. 제 얘기 한 번만 들어 주시죠.”
 58|
 59|“네놈이 무슨 말을 한다 해도 바뀌는 건 없다.”
 60|
 61|“흉수를 처치해 준다고 해도 말입니까?”
 62|
 63|“뭐라?”
 64|
 65|“독왕 당사문 대협을 해친 흉수 말입니다.”
 66|
 67|다음 순간.
 68|
 69|“이 핏덩이 같은 놈이 보자 보자 하니……!”
 70|
 71|쏴아아아.
 72|
 73|당사독의 전신으로부터 녹색 기운이 아지랑이처럼 솟구쳤다. 이글거리는 눈빛으로 나를 노려보던 그가 착 가라앉은 목소리로 말했다.
 74|
 75|“정녕 죽고 싶은 것이냐?”
 76|
 77|“앞길 창창한데 죽고 싶지는 않죠.”
 78|
 79|“놈을 치죄(治罪)하는 것은 본가의 몫이다. 그런데 감히 너 같은 외인 따위가!”
 80|
 81|후우우웅!
 82|
 83|광풍 같은 기세가 일어나 전각을 뒤흔든다. 나는 몸을 부르르 떠는 신의와 문경의 앞을 가로막으며 대답했다.
 84|
 85|“그래서 그 결과는 어떻게 됐습니까?”
 86|
 87|“……!”
 88|
 89|“흉수는 천하의 독왕을 쓰러트릴 만큼 엄청난 고수입니다. 게다가 다른 곳도 아닌 사천에서 당문의 이목을 벗어나 아미파에서 혈사를 일으킬 정도니 강한 건 무공뿐만이 아닐 거고요.”
 90|
 91|사천 땅이 아무리 넓다 하지만, 장구한 세월 동안 당문이 뿌리내린 곳.
 92|
 93|이건 집 앞마당에서 가문의 원수를 놓친 것과 같다. 가솔의 대부분을 이끌고 추적에 나섰음에도 빈손으로 돌아와야 했던 당사독의 얼굴이 딱딱하게 굳었다.
 94|
 95|“지금, 본가의 무능을 탓하는 것이냐?”
 96|
 97|“그럴 리가요.”
 98|
 99|사천당문이 무능하다면 천하에 산재한 문파 대부분은 빗장 걸고 봉문 해야지.
100|
101|구파일방, 오대세가로 불리는 그들은 그야말로 무림을 지탱하는 거인들이다. 지금의 사태는 사천당문과 아미파가 무능한 것이 아니라, 흉수라는 놈이 괴물인 거다.
102|
103|“가능성을 말씀드리는 겁니다.”
104|
105|“가능성?”
106|
107|“놈은 십왕(十王)에 비견할 수 있는 무공에 도주에도 일가견이 있습니다. 돕는 손이 늘어나면 잡을 수 있는 가능성도 높아지지 않겠습니까?”
108|
109|“본가의 녹영대가 이미 놈을 쫓고 있다. 노부도 만일의 사태에 대비하여 잠시 귀환했을 뿐, 머지않아 반드시 놈을 추살 할 것이다.”
110|
111|당사독이 날카로운 눈빛으로 나와 청풍을 훑었다.
112|
113|“본가는 대사천당문. 외인의 도움은 필요치 않다. 너희 같은 핏덩이들은 더더욱.”
114|
115|“……아, 음. 예.”
116|
117|글쎄. 나 정도면 후기지수 수준은 이미 까마득하게 벗어나지 않았나 싶은데.
118|
119|‘특히 저 녀석은.’
120|
121|멀뚱멀뚱 구경만 하는 청풍을 힐끗 바라본 나는 뒤통수를 긁적였다.
122|
123|‘음. 대충 이렇게 될 것 같긴 했는데.’
124|
125|개썅마이웨이를 지향하는 사천당문의 가풍(家風)을 생각해보면 이 정도는 충분히 예상했던 바다.
126|
127|그래서 나도 사천당문으로 오는 길에 더 매력적인 대책을 떠올린 거고.
128|
129|“그럼 어디서 굴러먹다 왔는지 모를 핏덩이들 말고, 화왕(火王)은 어떠십니까?”
130|
131|“……!”
132|
133|“어찌어찌 흉수를 추적해서 알아냈다 칩시다. 그럼 걔가 팔뚝 들이밀면서 빨리 정맥에 독바늘 쑤셔 넣어 주세요, 이러진 않을 거 아닙니까.”
134|
135|살려는 자. 죽이려는 자. 분명 치열한 혈전이 벌어질 수밖에 없다.
136|
137|사천당문이 전력을 다한다면 독왕의 복수는 할 수 있겠지만, 엄청난 피해 또한 각오해야 한다.
138|
139|방계든 직계든, 당문의 피를 이은 가솔들이 숱하게 죽어 나갈 것이다.
140|
141|“노야, 아니 스승님과 저희가 돕겠습니다. 사천당문의 피해를 최소화하고 흉수의 처분 또한 가주님께 맡기겠습니다.”
142|
143|“……불가. 어떤 피해를 감수하더라도 본가의 힘으로 해내야 한다.”
144|
145|“대답이 반 박자 늦으셨네요.”
146|
147|“이것이 선조들께서, 본가가 지금껏 걸어온 길이다. 그렇게 만든 사천당문이야!”
148|
149|“알고 있습니다. 사천당문이 어떤 길을 걸어왔는지는.”
150|
151|핏줄로 이어진 끈끈한 혈족(血族)들. 한 번 맺은 원한은 절대 잊지 않으며 보복은 냉혹하다.
152|
153|그것이 사천당가가 걸어온 길이고, 사람들이 존경과 동시에 두려워하는 이유였다.
154|
155|나는 나직한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
156|
157|“하지만 가끔 지름길로 간다고 해서 사람들이 손가락질하지는 않을 겁니다. 그 지름길을 선택한 이유가 가솔들의 희생을 줄이기 위해서라면 더더욱.”
158|
159|당사독이 입술을 질끈 깨물었다.
160|
161|어쩌면 그는 보이는 것만큼 냉혹한 사람이 아닐지 모른다.
162|
163|아니, 설령 그렇다 하더라도 복수만을 우선시하는 냉혹한 가주는 아닐 것이다.
164|
165|‘그랬다면 가문으로 돌아오지도 않았을 테니까.’
166|
167|하지만 만독수라 당사독은 돌아왔다. 혹시 모를 일말의 위험으로부터 가문을 지키기 위해, 자신이 떠난 후 가문에 남겨진 힘없는 가솔들을 지키기 위해.
168|
169|“어떻게 하시겠습니까?”
170|
171|물음에 대한 답이 들려온 것은, 그로부터 한참이 흐른 후였다.
172|
173|“……만약, 아주 만약에 만독지환이 있다면 적 대협을 치료할 수 있겠느냐?”
174|
175|“제가 아는 어느 분 말로는 그렇다던데요.”
176|
177|내 눈짓에 신의가 입을 열었다.
178|
179|“이미 준비는 거의 끝났습니다. 만독지환이 더해진다면, 치료에는 아무 문제가 없을겁니다.”
180|
181|“얼마나 걸리겠소?”
182|
183|“보름. 보름이면 충분하지요.”
184|
185|“보름…….”
186|
187|낮게 침음성을 흘린 당사독이 신의를 바라보며 말했다.
188|
189|“노부 역시 일전에 적 대협의 병세를 살펴본 적이 있소. 내 비록 독공에 비해 의술이 일천 하다고는 하나, 도무지 어떤 증세인지 알 수 없더군. 정말 가능하겠소?”
190|
191|“가능합니다.”
192|
193|순간 울려 퍼진 맑은 목소리.
194|
195|한 걸음 앞으로 나선 문경이 한 마디를 덧붙였다.
196|
197|“신의라면, 가능합니다.”
198|
199|“맹랑한 녀석이로고. 그대의 제자요?”
200|
201|당사독의 물음에 희미하게 웃는 것으로 답을 대신한 신의가 입을 열었다.
202|
203|“환자의 회생을 위해서는 반드시 만독지환이 있어야 합니다. 신물을 숨기고픈 마음을 이해하나, 부디 넓은 아량으로 인의(人意)를 베푸시지요.”
204|
205|“인의라. 네 녀석도 그리 생각하느냐?”
206|
207|“갑자기요?”
208|
209|“말하거라. 네 생각을 듣고 싶다.”
210|
211|“굳이 그러시다면야.”
212|
213|어깨를 으쓱해 보인 내가 대답했다.
214|
215|“인의보다는 은원(恩怨)이라고 해 두시죠.”
216|
217|“이유는?”
218|
219|“무림이니까. 누군가 도움을 준다면 보답하는 것이 강호의 도리 아닙니까.”
220|
221|당사독의 주름진 입가에 슬쩍 미소가 떠올랐다.
222|
223|“훨씬 듣기 좋군.”
224|
225|“듣기에도 좋고, 입에 발린 소리도 아닙니다.”
226|
227|“만약 적 대협이 치료받는 사이 흉수가 이역만리로 도망친다면 어쩌겠느냐?”
228|
229|“저 혼자서라도 놈을 추격해서 잡아 오겠습니다. 아, 물론 당장 가겠다는 소리는 아닙니다. 스승님이 깨어나실 때까지는 꿈쩍도 안 할 거라서요.”
230|
231|“웃긴 놈이군. 흉수는 찢어 죽여도 시원찮을 놈이지만, 엄청난 고수다. 그런 놈을 너 같은 핏덩이가 사로잡을 수 있겠느냐?”
232|
233|“도저히 사로잡지 못할 것 같으면 죽여야죠.”
234|
235|“으하, 으하하하!”
236|
237|한바탕 광소를 터트린 당사독이 웃음을 그치고 한마디를 툭 내뱉었다.
238|
239|“만독지환은 존재하지 않는다.”
240|
241|“……예?”
242|
243|아니 시벌, 이게 무슨 소리야.
244|
245|이 늙은이가 지금까지 날 갖고 논 건가?
246|
247|뒤통수가 얼얼해지는 것을 느끼고 있던 그때, 당사독의 목소리가 이어졌다.
248|
249|“만독지환은 그저 낡은 전설일 뿐이다. 본가의 혈족들 사이에서도 케케묵은 이야기야.”
250|
251|“아니, 없어요? 진짜 없어요?”
252|
253|“아무도 모르고, 누구도 알아서는 안 된다.”
254|
255|“시부럴 거. 그럼 처음부터 그렇게 얘기를 하시든가! 지금 저랑 장난합…….”
256|
257|쉬이이익.
258|
259|나는 말을 잇지 못하고 입을 다물었다.
260|
261|당사독의 품 안에서 스르륵 기어 나온 새하얀 뱀 한 마리가 혀를 날름거리며 나를 빤히 바라보고 있었기 때문이다.
262|
263|‘저건 또 뭐야.’
264|
265|볼드모트도 아니고. 여기서 갑자기 뱀이 왜 나와.
266|
267|심지어 뱀답지 않게 뿔도 달려 있다. 내가 뱀의 까만 눈동자를 마주 노려보던 그때, 신의가 신음처럼 중얼거렸다.
268|
269|“천년독각사……?”
270|
271|이름부터 아주 독사답다.
272|
273|슬그머니 뒷걸음질 치는 나를 보며 피식 웃은 당사독이 뱀의 세모꼴 머리를 쓰다듬었다.
274|
275|“겁먹기는. 위험한 녀석이 아니니 물러설 것 없다.”
276|
277|“이름부터 존나 위험해 보이는데요.”
278|
279|“천년독각사?”
280|
281|“네. 무슨 이름이 골든래트리버도 아니고 천년독각사를…… 됐고요. 만독지환, 진짜 없습니까?”
282|
283|“천년독각사가 아니라 미미다.”
284|
285|“예?”
286|
287|“당미미. 이 녀석에게 내가 붙여 준 이름이지.”
288|
289|뭐야, 그게. 무서워…….
290|
291|애정이 듬뿍 담긴 손길로 미미쨩을 쓰다듬던 당사독이 문득 신의를 바라봤다.
292|
293|“그대라면 알고 있을 거요. 이 녀석이 평범한 천년독각사가 아니라는 것을.”
294|
295|신의가 고개를 끄덕였다.
296|
297|“천년독각사는 극독을 품은 희귀한 독물(毒物)로, 몸통은 온통 검은 빛이며 성정이 매우 흉포하여 결코 길들일 수 없는 것으로 알고 있습니다. 한데…….”
298|
299|“보는 바와 같소. 이 녀석은 생김새도 다르거니와, 성정도 매우 온순하오.”
300|
301|“하지만 언제 돌변할지 모릅니다. 한 방울의 독으로도 백 마리의 소를 죽일 수 있는 독물 아닙니까.”
302|

“Because this is the Murim. If someone helps you, isn’t it the way of the martial world to repay them?”

[P111]
A faint smile touched the corner of Tang Sadok’s wrinkled mouth.

[P112]
“That is far more pleasing to hear.”

[P113]
“It sounds better, and it isn’t empty flattery.”

[P114]
“What will you do if the culprit flees to some distant foreign land while Great Hero Jeok is being treated?”

[P115]
“I’ll chase him down myself and bring him back. Ah, I’m not saying I’ll leave right away, of course. I won’t budge until my Master wakes up.”

[P116]
“You’re an amusing bastard. The culprit deserves to be torn limb from limb, but he is also an extraordinary master. Do you truly believe a greenhorn like you can capture him?”

[P117]
“If I can’t take him alive, I’ll kill him.”

[P118]
“Ha… Hahahaha!”

[P119]
Tang Sadok burst into uproarious laughter. When it finally subsided, he tossed out a casual remark.

[P120]
“The Myriad-Poison Ring does not exist.”

[P121]
“…What?”

[P122]
What the fuck was he talking about?

[P123]
Had this old man been playing me the entire time?

[P124]
As the back of my head went numb, Tang Sadok continued.

[P125]
“The Myriad-Poison Ring is nothing more than an old legend. Even among our blood relatives, it is merely an ancient tale.”

[P126]
“What do you mean, it doesn’t exist? It really doesn’t?”

[P127]
“No one knows, and no one must ever know.”

[P128]
“Fuck! Then you should have said that from the beginning! Have you been messing with me this whole—”

[P129]
Ssssss.

[P130]
I snapped my mouth shut before I could finish.

[P131]
A pure-white snake had slowly crawled out of Tang Sadok’s robes and was staring fixedly at me, its tongue flicking.

[P132]
*What the hell is that?*

[P133]
What was he, Voldemort? Why was a snake suddenly coming out of his clothes?

[P134]
It even had horns, which no normal snake had. As I stared into its black eyes, the Divine Physician murmured in disbelief.

[P135]
“A Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake…?”

[P136]
Even the name sounded lethally venomous.

[P137]
Tang Sadok laughed quietly when he saw me edging backward and stroked the snake’s triangular head.

[P138]
“Don’t be afraid. It isn’t dangerous, so there’s no need to retreat.”

[P139]
“Its name sounds fucking dangerous.”

[P140]
“Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake?”

[P141]
“Yes. What kind of name is that? It’s not like you’re calling it a golden retriever. Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake… Never mind. Does the Myriad-Poison Ring really not exist?”

[P142]
“It isn’t called Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake. Its name is Mimi.”

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
“Tang Mimi. That is the name I gave her.”

[P145]
What the hell? That was terrifying…

[P146]
As Tang Sadok lovingly stroked Mimi-chan, he suddenly looked at the Divine Physician.

[P147]
“You must know that this creature is no ordinary Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake.”

[P148]
The Divine Physician nodded.

[P149]
“As I understand it, the Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake is an extremely rare and venomous creature. Its entire body is black, and its temperament is so ferocious that it can never be tamed. And yet…”

[P150]
“As you can see, this one looks different and has an exceptionally gentle disposition.”

[P151]
“But you cannot know when it might suddenly turn on you. Is it not a venomous creature whose single drop of poison could kill a hundred cows?”

[P152]
“There is no need to worry. This one has no venom.”

[P153]
“What?”

[P154]
“To be precise… it would be more accurate to say that her venom is gone.”

[P155]

[P156]
It lasted only a moment, but they had clearly communicated. The clever snake had understood its master’s intentions.

[P157]
Hiss! Ssssss!

[P158]
She lowered her head with a metallic hiss and spat something onto Tang Sadok’s palm.

[P159]
It landed with a soft plop, emerging from the slime that coated it.

[P160]
*That’s…*

[P161]
A ring.

[P162]
Set into it was a black gemstone that seemed to contain all the darkness in the world.

[P163]

[P164]
“No way…”

[P165]

[P166]
“Remember this. No one knows, and no one must ever know.”

[P167]
“Then…”

[P168]
“Yes.”

[P169]
Tang Sadok held it out to me.

[P170]
“This is our family’s sacred artifact.”

[P171]

Ding.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

[P116]
“You’re an amusing bastard. The culprit deserves to be torn limb from limb, but he is also an extraordinary master. Do you truly believe a greenhorn like you can capture him?”

[P117]
“If I can’t take him alive, I’ll kill him.”

[P118]
“Ha… Hahahaha!”

[P119]
Tang Sadok burst into uproarious laughter. When it finally subsided, he tossed out a casual remark.

[P120]
“The Myriad-Poison Ring does not exist.”

[P121]
“…What?”

[P122]
What the fuck was he talking about?

[P123]
Had this old man been playing me the entire time?

[P124]
As the back of my head went numb, Tang Sadok continued.

[P125]
“The Myriad-Poison Ring is nothing more than an old legend. Even among our blood relatives, it is merely an ancient tale.”

[P126]
“What do you mean, it doesn’t exist? It really doesn’t?”

[P127]
“No one knows, and no one must ever know.”

[P128]
“Fuck! Then you should have said that from the beginning! Have you been messing with me this whole—”

[P129]
Ssssss.

[P130]
I snapped my mouth shut before I could finish.

[P131]
A pure-white snake had slowly crawled out of Tang Sadok’s robes and was staring fixedly at me, its tongue flicking.

[P132]
*What the hell is that?*

[P133]
What was he, Voldemort? Why was a snake suddenly coming out of his clothes?

[P134]

[P135]
“A Thousand-Year Poison Horned Snake…?”

[P136]

[P137]

[P138]

[P139]

[P140]

[P142]

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]

[P145]

[P146]

[P147]

[P148]

[P149]

[P151]

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
